references.text: Psalm 105:25 describes how God turned the hearts of the Egyptians to hate his people and act cunningly against his servants, which directly refers to Pharaoh's plan in Exodus 1:10.
Psalm 83:4-5 describes enemies who devise cunning plans against God's people and seek to wipe them out as a nation, reflecting Pharaoh's intention to deal wisely with the Israelites.
Proverbs 21:30 teaches that no wisdom, understanding, or counsel can prevail against the Lord, which stands in contrast to Pharaoh's attempt to act 'wisely' against God's people.
Stephen quotes this event in his speech and describes how a new king used cunning against the Israelites and mistreated their ancestors.
Verse 7 provides the background for Pharaoh's fear by describing how the Israelites became numerous and powerful, which motivated his cunning plan.
Verse 12 shows that Pharaoh's plan failed, for the more they oppressed the Israelites, the more they multiplied and spread.
God's prophecy to Abraham that his descendants would be strangers and oppressed in a foreign land for 400 years, but that the nation oppressing them will be judged.
Contrasting strategies for dealing with foreign peoples in the land: integration/exploitation (Shechem) versus oppression/fear (Egypt).
Parallel fear among foreign powers (Balak/Egypt) regarding Israel's growth and desperate strategies to stop them.
Theological contrast: Fear leads to oppression (Egypt) versus trust in God overcoming fear of enemies (Hezekiah).
Contrast in dealing with enemies: Oppression for one's own security (Egypt) versus spreading for God's glory (Psalm).
